The shoe is whole at x 46-1033, y 264-781 (measured), clear of the logo, which stays legible on the template's top grey gradient. Headline: 3 lines, 84 px, white, top 998, well below the sole; one left edge (x 50/52/52). The comma in '$190,' ends at x 995 and the vertical credit 'Image: Carhartt WIP' starts at x 1023, a 28 px gap, so they don't touch. The ~200 px gradient between sole and headline reads as product-shot breathing room, not an empty band. Slides 2-4: white Title Case labels; labels and bullets share the x 72 edge; no overlap or overflow; the 'f' in '0 of 4' stops about 23 px above the label; Sources lines readable; render report shows no credit_collision. Tag carharttwip has evidence in meta.json. Facts verified at G1/G2: Nike launch page IW6306-200 'Light British Tan and Twilight Marsh' $190 'Available 11/20'; Carhartt WIP 43J page $190, Half Dome, canvas, suede and leather, Air Max heel; Sole Retriever codes and Twilight Marsh exclusive; Complex 12 Nov early release in select stores, 20 Nov SNKRS. The pictured 43J pair matches Nike's own -200 imagery (same tan nubuck, olive ribbed canvas, black Air sole). Weak checks: hook 1 and send 1, because this is a foreign collab with no India release (learnings cap); the $190 and 20 Nov on the cover are specific but don't stop an Indian scroll the way a ₹ price at Superkicks would, and the forward audience is a narrow group of import buyers. Strong: keep (dates, $190, both SNKRS style codes, which pair is exclusive, the time-stamped India check); reply (a shipping-in question that fits the no-India-release angle); original (idly's own four-store India check, official credited image); alone (every slide names the shoe). Read 2, borderline: slide 3's Half Dome and materials bullets are description rather than reader utility, but they say what the shoe is, which a drop post needs. Zero margin at 12.
